questions.q: What must exist on every instance before an Availability Group can be created at all?
options: A database mirroring endpoint (Hadr_endpoint), listening on a TCP port such as 5022
A Failover Cluster Instance
A completed log shipping configuration
A listener, created before the availability group itself
questions.explain: AGs reuse the endpoint mechanism from database mirroring — every replica-hosting instance needs one before joining an AG.

questions.q: Why are SQLPRD01 and SQLPRD02 both configured as SYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT with FAILOVER_MODE = AUTOMATIC?
options: They're close together (same metro area, low latency), so they can safely commit synchronously and fail over to each other automatically within seconds
Automatic failover is required for every replica in any Availability Group
Synchronous commit is only possible between exactly two replicas
SQLPRD02 is the DR replica in this scenario
questions.explain: Low latency between the two Columbus datacenters makes synchronous commit practical, which is what enables safe automatic failover between them.

questions.q: Why is SQLDR01 configured as ASYNCHRONOUS_COMMIT with FAILOVER_MODE = MANUAL instead?
options: The ~175-mile distance makes synchronous commit impractical, and manual failover ensures a human confirms a real disaster before promoting a replica that may be behind
SQLDR01 doesn't support any other configuration
Manual failover mode disables asynchronous commit
There is no meaningful difference between SQLDR01's configuration and the other two replicas
questions.explain: Distance rules out synchronous commit, and manual failover mode is the deliberate safeguard against an automatic failover to a replica with unknown data loss.

questions.q: What does granting CREATE ANY DATABASE on the AG enable?
options: Automatic seeding — SQL Server streams the initial database data to the new secondary directly, instead of a manual backup/restore
It allows any user to create new databases on the secondary
It disables the need for a listener
It is required only for asynchronous replicas
questions.explain: Automatic seeding is the real Always On feature this permission enables, replacing the older manual full-backup-with-NORECOVERY seeding process.

questions.q: What problem does the listener (BHFS-AGL) actually solve for Bellhaven?
options: It gives applications one stable virtual network name to connect to, which SQL Server routes to whichever replica currently holds the primary role
It replaces the need for a backup strategy
It is only used for reporting queries, never for the main application
It physically moves the database files between replicas during failover
questions.explain: The listener means connection strings never need to change after a failover — they always point to BHFS-AGL, and SQL Server redirects to the current primary.
